GOLDEN FIXTURE PROVENANCE
=========================

Every file in this directory is a HiLink response body copied from a third-party corpus of real
device captures. Nothing here was written from what the client "expects" to see. The whole point of
this directory is that the client and the simulator in internal/device/sim are written by the same
author, so if the XML were invented both sides would agree with each other and both be wrong.

Firmware quirks that are preserved deliberately and must never be "fixed":

  - MaxIdelTime is misspelled in the firmware. Unit is SECONDS. Keep the spelling verbatim.
  - Element order is the device's order, not alphabetical and not our struct order.
  - Empty elements are written <Tag></Tag>, not <Tag/>, everywhere except the one compact error
    sample noted below, which is how one corpus captured it.
  - The device answers HTTP 200 with Content-Type: text/html even when the body is <error>.
    Status code carries no information. Always parse the body.
  - monitoring/status omits WanIPAddress entirely on some firmware builds (see the two variants).
  - dhcp/settings carries accessipaddress and homeurl in addition to the ten documented fields.


SUCCESS RESPONSES
-----------------

webserver_sestokinfo.xml
    "Hacking Huawei E3372 HiLink" - blog.idorobots.org
    https://blog.idorobots.org/entries/hacking-huawei-e3372-hilink..html
    Device: E3372 HiLink. The SesInfo value is elided as "SessionID=..." in the original post;
    the element structure and the TokInfo value are verbatim.

device_information.xml
    dubanoze/hilink, e3372h.py, docstring of device_information()
    https://github.com/dubanoze/hilink/blob/master/e3372h.py
    Device: E3372, HardwareVersion CL2E3372HM, SoftwareVersion 22.317.01.00.00.
    This is the closest capture available to the hardware this project targets.

device_basic_information.xml
    dubanoze/hilink, e3372h.py, docstring of basic_info(). Same device.

device_signal.xml
    "Huawei E5186 AJAX API" - Jari Turkia, blog.hqcodeshop.fi
    https://blog.hqcodeshop.fi/archives/247-Huawei-E5186-AJAX-API.html
    Device: E5186s-22a. Kept because it is the only capture with populated signal values, which is
    what exercises the dBm/dB unit-suffix parser.

device_signal_e3372.xml
    dubanoze/hilink, e3372h.py, docstring of device_signal(). Device: E3372.
    All signal fields empty because the device was on WCDMA. This is the shape the parser must
    survive without erroring, and it carries psatt/lte_bandwidth/lte_bandinfo which the E5186 lacks.

monitoring_status.xml
    vzakharchenko/huawei-hilink (npm huawei-hilink), README.md, output of
    `huawei-hilink monitoring --exportFile=status.xml --exportFormat=xml`
    https://github.com/vzakharchenko/huawei-hilink
    Device: E3372h-320, firmware 11.0.1.1(H697SP1C983), WebUI 11.0.1.1(W13SP2C7201).
    Note this firmware build has NO WanIPAddress element at all.

monitoring_status_wanip.xml
    dubanoze/hilink, e3372h.py, docstring of monitoring_status(). Device: E3372.
    This build DOES carry WanIPAddress. Both variants are kept because the client must not require
    the element and the simulator must be able to serve either.

monitoring_traffic_statistics.xml
    dubanoze/hilink, e3372h.py, docstring of traffic_statistics(). Device: E3372.

monitoring_month_statistics.xml
    "Huawei Modem API and Data Plan Monitor" - mrt-prodz.com
    https://www.mrt-prodz.com/blog/view/2015/05/huawei-modem-api-and-data-plan-monitor/
    Single-line, no whitespace between elements - that is how the device sent it and how it is
    stored here. MonthLastClearTime is "2015-4-28": unpadded, not ISO 8601. Do not normalise it.

dialup_connection.xml
    dubanoze/hilink, e3372h.py, docstring of dialup_connection(). Device: E3372.
    Independently corroborated at MaxIdelTime=600 by blog.hqcodeshop.fi (E5186) and at 7200/86400
    by blog.idorobots.org (E3372). The misspelling is present in all three captures.

dialup_mobile_dataswitch.xml
    blog.hqcodeshop.fi E5186 AJAX API table, /api/dialup/mobile-dataswitch GET.

net_current_plmn.xml
    dubanoze/hilink, e3372h.py, docstring of current_plmn(). Device: E3372, Beeline KZ, Rat 2.

net_register.xml
    HSPDev/Huawei-E5180-API README and if0xx/Huawei-Hilink-API README, both showing the same
    capture rendered through PHP var_dump of SimpleXMLElement.
    https://github.com/HSPDev/Huawei-E5180-API
    https://github.com/if0xx/Huawei-Hilink-API
    Values verbatim (3 DK / 23806 / Rat 2); re-serialised from var_dump back to the XML the device
    sent, because var_dump is a rendering of the parse, not of the wire bytes.

net_net_mode.xml
    dubanoze/hilink, e3372h.py, docstring of net_mode(). Device: E3372.
    NetworkMode "01" = 2G only. Code table primary source:
    Salamek/huawei-lte-api huawei_lte_api/enums/net.py NetworkModeEnum
    ("00" auto, "01" 2G only, "02" 3G only, "03" 4G only).

pin_status.xml
    dubanoze/hilink, e3372h.py, docstring of pin_status(). Device: E3372.
    Identical capture also in the blog.hqcodeshop.fi E5186 table.

sms_sms_list.xml
    Narf-AI/huawei-lte-api (crates.io huawei-dongle-api 0.2.1),
    src/models/sms.rs test_sms_list_response_multiple_messages.
    https://github.com/Narf-AI/huawei-lte-api
    Real device capture: indices 40003/40002, dates 2025-06-09 and 2024-11-22, a real MSISDN and a
    shortcode sender. Field casing here (Smstat/Index/Phone/Content/Date/Sca/SaveType/Priority/
    SmsType) is the sms/sms-list casing and differs from the lowercase casing that
    sms/sms-list-phone returns - see the note at the bottom.

sms_sms_list_empty.xml
    Empty-inbox shape from HSPDev/Huawei-E5180-API and if0xx/Huawei-Hilink-API READMEs
    (Count 0, empty Messages container).

sms_sms_list_fragment.xml
    Narf-AI/huawei-lte-api src/models/sms.rs test_sms_list_response_missing_count, with SmsType
    changed from 1 to 2 - this is the ONE success fixture with a substituted value, and it is
    substituted only in that single field. SmsType 2 = MULTIPART per the primary source
    Salamek/huawei-lte-api huawei_lte_api/enums/sms.py TypeEnum. No third-party corpus publishes a
    captured multipart fragment, so the envelope is real and the discriminator value comes from the
    enum table.

dhcp_settings.xml
    Element ORDER is verbatim from tnbhaeufi/Huawei-E3372h-320-IP-Range-change script.txt, a
    bookmarklet that reads the device's dhcp/settings and POSTs it back with two octets changed.
    https://github.com/tnbhaeufi/Huawei-E3372h-320-IP-Range-change
    Device: E3372h-320. That order is corroborated field-for-field by Narf-AI/huawei-lte-api
    src/models/dhcp.rs DhcpSettings, which was derived from a real device.
    Values are the factory defaults (192.168.8.0/24, lease 86400).
    accessipaddress and homeurl appear in the real payload and are preserved.

response_ok.xml
    The universal set-response. Captured in Narf-AI/huawei-lte-api src/models/common.rs
    (`<response>OK</response>`) and in nicw0rm/huawei README. Also the primary source
    Salamek/huawei-lte-api huawei_lte_api/enums/client.py ResponseEnum.OK = "OK".


ERROR RESPONSES
---------------

The error envelope is identical for every code; only the integer changes. Two independent verbatim
captures of the envelope exist:

  (A) pretty form, one element per line, empty <message></message>
      - arska/e3372 issue #1, POST to /api/dialup/mobile-dataswitch returning code 125002
        https://github.com/arska/e3372/issues/1
      - Salamek/huawei-lte-api discussion #190, user arekm, returning code 100010
        https://github.com/Salamek/huawei-lte-api/discussions/190
        (that capture is stored here verbatim as error_100010.xml)

  (B) compact form on one line with a self-closing <message/>
      - Narf-AI/huawei-lte-api src/models/common.rs test_check_for_api_error, code 125003
        stored here verbatim as error_125003_compact.xml

error_125002.xml   envelope (A) verbatim from arska/e3372 issue #1. Nothing substituted.
error_100010.xml   envelope (A) verbatim from huawei-lte-api discussion #190. Nothing substituted.
error_125003_compact.xml
                   envelope (B) verbatim from Narf-AI/huawei-lte-api. Nothing substituted.

The remaining error files are envelope (A) with the code integer taken from the firmware error
constant table. They are NOT invented codes - each integer is attested by a primary source:

error_100002.xml   ERROR_NOT_SUPPORT
error_100003.xml   ERROR_NO_RIGHT           (this is "login required", NOT 100002)
error_100004.xml   ERROR_BUSY / ERROR_SYSTEM_BUSY
error_100005.xml   ERROR_FORMAT_ERROR
error_108003.xml   ERROR_LOGIN_ALREADY_LOGINED
error_112001.xml   ERROR_SET_NET_MODE_AND_BAND_WHEN_DAILUP_FAILED
error_125003.xml   ERROR_WRONG_SESSION_TOKEN (pretty form of the compact capture above)

    Primary source 1: Salamek/huawei-lte-api huawei_lte_api/enums/client.py ResponseCodeEnum
        https://github.com/Salamek/huawei-lte-api/blob/master/huawei_lte_api/enums/client.py
        100001 ERROR_SYSTEM_UNKNOWN   100002 ERROR_SYSTEM_NO_SUPPORT  100003 ERROR_SYSTEM_NO_RIGHTS
        100004 ERROR_SYSTEM_BUSY      100005 ERROR_FORMAT_ERROR       120001 ERROR_VOICE_BUSY
        125001 ERROR_WRONG_TOKEN      125002 ERROR_SYSTEM_CSRF        125003 ERROR_WRONG_SESSION_TOKEN

    Primary source 2: HSPDev/Huawei-E5180-API README, the full firmware error constant table lifted
    out of the WebUI. https://github.com/HSPDev/Huawei-E5180-API
        ERROR_NOT_SUPPORT = 100002
        ERROR_NO_RIGHT = 100003
        ERROR_BUSY = 100004
        ERROR_FORMAT_ERROR = 100005
        ERROR_PARAMETER_ERROR = 100006
        ERROR_LOGIN_NO_EXIST_USER = 108001
        ERROR_LOGIN_PASSWORD_ERROR = 108002
        ERROR_LOGIN_ALREADY_LOGINED = 108003
        ERROR_LOGIN_MODIFY_PASSWORD_FAILED = 108004
        ERROR_LOGIN_TOO_MANY_USERS_LOGINED = 108005
        ERROR_LOGIN_USERNAME_OR_PASSWORD_ERROR = 108006
        ERROR_LOGIN_TOO_MANY_TIMES = 108007
        ERROR_SET_NET_MODE_AND_BAND_WHEN_DAILUP_FAILED = 112001
        ERROR_SET_NET_SEARCH_MODE_WHEN_DAILUP_FAILED = 112002
        ERROR_SET_NET_MODE_AND_BAND_FAILED = 112003
        ERROR_SET_NET_SEARCH_MODE_FAILED = 112004
        ERROR_NET_REGISTER_NET_FAILED = 112005
        ERROR_NET_SIM_CARD_NOT_READY_STATUS = 112008
        ERROR_UNKNOWN = 100001

    Note for whoever owns internal/domain/errors.go: 100006 (ERROR_PARAMETER_ERROR) DOES exist in
    the firmware table above. CONVENTIONS.md section 5 states it does not. It is absent from
    huawei-lte-api's ResponseCodeEnum, which is a curated subset, not the full firmware table.


SIM STATE CODES
---------------

    Primary source: zbchristian/huawei_hilink_api, huawei_hilink_api.sh, _enableSIM()
    https://github.com/zbchristian/huawei_hilink_api

        255  no SIM
        256  CPIN error
        257  ready
        258  PIN disabled
        259  check PIN (verification in progress)
        260  PIN required
        261  PUK required

    261 is PUK REQUIRED. It is not a combined "PIN and PUK locked" state.


SMS FIELD CASING
----------------

Two different casings exist and they are not interchangeable:

    sms/sms-list          <Count> <Messages><Message> <Smstat> <Index> <Phone> <Content> <Date>
                          <Sca> <SaveType> <Priority> <SmsType>
                          Attested by Narf-AI/huawei-lte-api, HSPDev/Huawei-E5180-API,
                          if0xx/Huawei-Hilink-API, and Salamek/huawei-lte-api Sms.Message.from_dict.

    sms/sms-list-phone    <count> <messages><message> <smstat> <index> <phone> <content> <date>
    sms/sms-list-contact  <sca> <curbox> <savetype> <priority> <smstype> <unreadcount>
                          Attested by vzakharchenko/huawei-hilink README.
                          These two endpoints are out of scope for v1; the casing is recorded here
                          only so nobody "corrects" sms/sms-list to match them.


REQUEST BODIES (not responses, kept for encoder fidelity)
---------------------------------------------------------

dhcp/settings POST, real payload from tnbhaeufi/Huawei-E3372h-320-IP-Range-change:

    <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><request><DnsStatus>1</DnsStatus><DhcpStartIPAddress>
    192.168.N.100</DhcpStartIPAddress><DhcpIPAddress>192.168.N.1</DhcpIPAddress><accessipaddress>
    </accessipaddress><homeurl>hi.link</homeurl><DhcpStatus>1</DhcpStatus><DhcpLanNetmask>
    255.255.255.0</DhcpLanNetmask><SecondaryDns>192.168.N.1</SecondaryDns><PrimaryDns>192.168.N.1
    </PrimaryDns><DhcpEndIPAddress>192.168.N.100</DhcpEndIPAddress><DhcpLeaseTime>86400
    </DhcpLeaseTime></request>

    The ten-field form this project sends is the one from Salamek/huawei-lte-api
    huawei_lte_api/api/Dhcp.py set_settings, which adds ShowDnsSetting:
        DhcpIPAddress DhcpLanNetmask DhcpStatus DhcpStartIPAddress DhcpEndIPAddress
        DhcpLeaseTime DnsStatus PrimaryDns SecondaryDns ShowDnsSetting
    Moving DhcpIPAddress to another /24 without moving DhcpStartIPAddress and DhcpEndIPAddress into
    the same /24 is what makes the device answer 100005.

sms/send-sms POST, from blog.idorobots.org:

    <?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?><request><Index>-1</Index><Phones><Phone>NUMBER</Phone>
    </Phones><Sca></Sca><Content>TEXT</Content><Length>-1</Length><Reserved>1</Reserved>
    <Date>-1</Date></request>

net/net-mode POST field order, from Salamek/huawei-lte-api Net.set_net_mode:
    NetworkMode NetworkBand LTEBand

net/register POST field order, from Salamek/huawei-lte-api Net.set_register:
    Mode Plmn Rat


TOKEN HANDSHAKE
---------------

    GET /api/webserver/SesTokInfo yields SesInfo (the SessionID cookie) and TokInfo (one token).
    Tokens are single-use.

    zbchristian/huawei_hilink_api huawei_hilink_api.sh:
        "store the list of 30 tokens. Each token is valid for a single request"
        the batch arrives in the __RequestVerificationToken RESPONSE header, '#'-separated.

    Salamek/huawei-lte-api huawei_lte_api/Session.py:
        a response may instead refresh the queue via __RequestVerificationTokenone and
        __RequestVerificationTokentwo, or via a plain __RequestVerificationToken.

    Both header shapes are implemented in session.go and both are served by internal/device/sim.
